relationships.subject: HSV-1
relationships.evidence_quote: Our results demonstrate that infection of ND7/23 cells with the HSV-1 strain McKrae with GFP expression (M-GFP) causes a significant decrease in sodium currents during latency establishment.

relationships.subject: TNF-alpha
relationships.evidence_quote: Exposure of ND7/23 cells to TNF-α during latency establishment reverses the effect of HSV-1, resulting in a significant increase in sodium current density.

relationships.subject: TNF-alpha
relationships.evidence_quote: TNF-α stimulation of ND7/23 cells increases p38 signaling.

relationships.subject: SB203580
relationships.evidence_quote: Inhibition of p38 signaling with SB203580 or SB202190 eliminates the stimulatory effect of TNF-α on sodium currents.

relationships.subject: TNF-alpha
relationships.evidence_quote: TNF-α alone appears to evoke a significant reduction in the expression of Nav1.3 and Nav1.7 transcripts (Fig. 4C, E).

key_findings: In HSV-1 latency-establishment model ND7/23 cells, sodium currents are reduced and TNF-α restores them via p38 signaling; IL-6 does not.
TNF-α did not change TTX sensitivity or I-V relationship but altered Nav subunit transcripts (reduced Nav1.3/1.7 alone; increased Nav1.1, 1.2, 1.6 after latency establishment).
